CHROMIUM: bluetooth/sco - Parse correct conn handle According to Core spec 5.4.3 HCI Synchronous Data Packets the Connection_Handle uses the first 12 bits of header. This change fixes the connection handle value. Otherwise if the succeeding 2 bits of packet status flag is set, it could result in connection look up failure and drop one SCO packet. BUG=chromium:980454 TEST=Test wideband speech headset, verify there's no error printed for 'SCO packet for unknown connection handle' Change-Id: Idab09b69de768fc4113476409c9435af730dae7b Signed-off-by: Hsin-Yu Chao <hychao@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1718627 Tested-by: Hsinyu Chao <hychao@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Hsinyu Chao <hychao@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Shyh-In Hwang <josephsih@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: bluetooth/sco - Keep HCI SCO packet header in transparent mode According to Core spec 5.4.3 HCI Synchronous Data Packets, when erroneous data reporting feature is enabled, controller sets the packet status flag to indicate if data is intact in the payload. For wide band speech mode using voice_transparent settings, user space wants to know the value of packet status flag for packet loss concealment. We shall not strip the HCI SCO packet header in this case. BUG=chromium:980454 TEST=Apply CRAS patches and test WBS headset. Verified the erroneous data reporting is working fine by flagging lost/partial data. Change-Id: If90925f605e5f67a2815bea4a875b3d05359a758 Signed-off-by: Hsin-Yu Chao <hychao@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1718628 Tested-by: Hsinyu Chao <hychao@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Hsinyu Chao <hychao@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Shyh-In Hwang <josephsih@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: bluetooth/sco - Check for NULL socket in receiving sco data When recv_scodata is called, the hci_conn may actually hold a NULL sock hence accessing the settings of sco_pinfo causes crash. Fix this by moving the hci_conn socket NULL check earlier, to make sure we access valid sco_pinfo settings before taking care of HCI SCO header and call to sco_recv_frame. BUG=chromium:980454 TEST=Repeatedly stress wideband speech with BT headset, verify kernel doesn't crash. Change-Id: Ibe91a46964919507c2c8db2788567a86ce600819 Signed-off-by: Hsin-Yu Chao <hychao@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1718629 Tested-by: Hsinyu Chao <hychao@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Hsinyu Chao <hychao@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Shyh-In Hwang <josephsih@chromium.org>

tast: Introduce os/exec-style interface for SSH. Properly using golang.org/x/crypto/ssh to run commands via SSH is difficult for several reasons: - The ssh package does not support context.Context. To avoid freezes, we need to use background goroutines carefully. - The ssh package only allows invoking shells. This is a natural restriction due to SSH protocol itself, but using this interface directly would lead to fragile programs with random shell escapes. To absorb these difficulties we need a wrapper. Today we have SSH.Run, SSH.Start, SSHCommandHandle for this purpose, but it does not resolve these two issues completely. This change introduces an os/exec-style interface that solves these issues. To keep this CL short, it does not modify the existing users of SSHCommandHandle, but modifies SSHCommandHandle itself to use the new Cmd internally. Next CL will remove SSHCommandHandle and update the callers to directly use the new Cmd. BUG=chromium:971024 TEST=fast_build.sh -T TEST=fast_build.sh && ~/go/bin/tast run betty arc.Boot Change-Id: I845e1610862efbc1f62a88b440bf98f2ec58d6d3 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1651227 Tested-by: Shuhei Takahashi <nya@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Shuhei Takahashi <nya@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Hidehiko Abe <hidehiko@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Keigo Oka <oka@chromium.org>
